replication.target_description: Cheung and Heine (2015) Study 3 replication: four-condition one-way ANCOVA controlling for political ideology. Condition comparison in perceived conscious control.

n.sample_role: Participants in the outcome-specific ANCOVA; analytic count not established. Report-wide final sample: 743 participants (candidate context only).
n.exclusions: Report-wide comprehension-check exclusions follow original criteria. Additional outcome/covariate missingness or exclusions for this ANCOVA are not documented.
n.location: Method, Participants; Replication Analysis, Perpetrator-relevant perceptions, conscious-control ANCOVA (canonical text has no page markers; supplied locator p. 4)
n.quote: We excluded those participants who failed a comprehension check based on the criteria used by Cheung and Heine (2015), resulting in a final sample size of n = 743 participants ... There was a significant main effect of Condition on perceived conscious control, F(3, 735) = 24.99

notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text contains the primary results report titled "A Replication of Cheung and Heine (2015)", authored by Jarret T. Crawford and nine named coauthors at The College of New Jersey. It explicitly identifies replication of Study 3, names the preregistration https://osf.io/a7hct/, and includes a registration response block at https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/e9d3k/ with the title matching the supplied Crawford reference. The report title differs from the registration title ("Syntax and output files for Cheung & Heine 2015 study 3 replication"); the text contains the report itself, not just preregistration or abstract material. This establishes substantive project/source correspondence within the supplied material; DOI is not printed in the report body. No PDF was supplied, so no rendered page inspection was possible. Target matched by explicitly named outcome and ANCOVA design, not numeric matching or row order. The inspected primary report supplies a final post-comprehension-check participant sample of 743, but does not explicitly identify the analytic N for this outcome-specific ANCOVA. The results give an F test and residual degrees of freedom; the thirteen outcomes have differing residual degrees of freedom. Neither the final recruitment/sample count nor degrees of freedom establishes this test's analytic N under the assigned rules. No explicit mutually exclusive final condition counts for this critical test are supplied. The full supplied report, figures, summary table and appended registration responses were inspected; no outcome-specific analytic N was located. Candidate 743 is the report-wide final participant count only and is not entered as analytic n. No N calculation performed; no inference from df. Only n_r was assigned; other side/fields are unassigned placeholders.
